pages.head: Welcome to the Future!
pages.html:
In The Year 2000!

A Future Adventure from Sandbox Software, 1992.

Everybody knows what the year 2000 will be like. Cars will fly. Robots will mow the lawn, walk the dog and fold the laundry. Dinner will come in a pill (the turkey kind, with stuffing). The aliens will land, and they will be very friendly. And best of all, every phone booth on every corner will be a Teleport-A-Phone: drop in a quarter, dial, and BZZZT! you're across town.

We made a game about it, so you don't have to wait eight whole years.

You are Dex Dynamo, age 11, of 42 Dome Circle, Hover Heights. You wrote the greatest science fair report in the solar system: THE POCKET TELEPHONE - a telephone so small you could carry it in your pocket. (Twenty pages! With diagrams!)

Then Sparky 3000, your robot dog, ate it.

The Science Fair is today at 3:00 PM. It is on the Moon. Get going!

pages.head: Getting Started
pages.html:
What you need

  • An IBM PC or compatible, 286 or faster
  • VGA graphics and 640K of memory
  • A hard disk
  • A Sound Blaster for music and digitized sound (the PC speaker works too)

Installing

Make a directory on your hard disk, for example C:\YEAR2000, copy every file from the disk into it, and type YEAR2000.

The title screen

The intro counts all the way from 1992 to the year 2000 for you. Press any key for the menu, which is on TV, naturally. Choose Play to begin, Read Storyline to see how Sparky ate the report, or Read Instructions for a quick reminder of the controls. Leave the menu alone and Dex will show you around Hover Heights by himself.

Your goal

Collect at least 20 pages of your report across six levels of the future, catch Sparky to get back the cover page, and turn everything in to the judges at the Moon School Science Fair.

pages.head: Controls
pages.html:
Arrow keys or W A S DWalk up, left, down and right (a joystick works too)
Q / EWalk diagonally up-left / up-right
7 9 1 3 on the number padWalk diagonally up-left, up-right, down-left, down-right
SpaceFire the Laser-Tag Zapper (once you have one)
F1Help
F2Status: your score, lives, hit points and how many quarters you have
F3 / F4Music / sound effects on and off
F5 / F6Save / load a game
EscQuit to the menu

Moving around

Pressing two arrows together won't walk you on a slant. That's what Q, E and the number pad's corner keys are for.

Walk into things to use them. Walk into a page to pick it up, into a phone booth door to dial, and into an arcade game to play it. Doors that need a key open by themselves when you have the key.

Glass tubes and moonwalk belts carry you along whether you like it or not - you can step off to the side. On the Moon, your moon suit makes you bound along a whole block at a time.

Tip: nobody can see how many quarters are in their pocket without looking. Press F2!

pages.head: Things of the Future
pages.html:
Report pageSparky chewed them up and spat them all over the future. The judges need 20. There are plenty more than that, so don't worry if you miss a few.
QuarterThe money of the future is the same as the money of the past. A Teleport-A-Phone call costs one quarter. So does an arcade game.
Food pillA complete turkey dinner in one capsule. Restores your hit points.
Laser-Tag ZapperFound in your own backyard. Stuns robots. Comes with a full charge.
BatteryMore charge for the Zapper. Size AA, of course - some things never change.
Hover-ColaThe soft drink of tomorrow. An extra life in every can.
Garage remoteOpens the garage gate to your backyard.
STAFF ONLY keycardOpens the loading dock at Mega Mall 2000.
Moon PassLets you through the airlock into Moon School.

Phone booths

There's one on every corner. Some are OUT OF ORDER and some just ring and ring, but the ones with a glass door work: walk into the door, it takes your quarter, and the booth fills with sparkles. Step inside to teleport.

pages.head: Friends and Robots
pages.html:
Friendly folks

Aliens live next door now and they love a hug. Walk into one for a hug that heals you, and they'll beam home happy. Grandma in Florida hugs too.

Robots (zappable)

  • Robo-mowers trim the lawns in neat little squares.
  • Robo-dogs want to play fetch. With you.
  • Paperboy-bots and the newspaper cannons deliver the morning news at 60 miles an hour.
  • Fax-bots, security robots, runaway hover carts and robot shoppers crowd the Skyway and the Mall.
  • Telemarketer robots at the phone exchange really want to talk to you about switching your long-distance company.

A robot that chases you short-circuits when it bumps you, but it hurts. Zap them first!

Things that don't stop for anybody

Flying cars (even Grandpa's old CitiCar), fax trucks, hoverboard kids, moon buggies and dinosaurs. A bump hurts once, then they honk and swerve past (or back off) and leave you be. A zap does the same, but it wastes a charge. Meteors just hurt. Get out of the way!

Other dangers

Laser fences blink on and off - walk through while they're off. Tar pits are sticky and hot. And watch the sky on the Moon.

pages.head: The Levels
pages.html:
1. Dome Sweet Dome

Hover Heights, where the domes are white and the lawns are mowed by robots. The garage remote is lost in the hedge garden; the Zapper is in your backyard. The Teleport-A-Phone is on the corner by the newspaper cannons. Grandpa's 1976½ CitiCar is plugged in by your dome: the car of tomorrow since the Bicentennial, one mile of range for every hour on the cord. Give it a honk.

2. The Information Superhighway

Everybody's been talking about it, and here it is: fourteen lanes of hover traffic hauling faxes through the clouds. Cross island by island. Ride the pneumatic tube if you're brave, and catch the latest on the Skyway News Feed along the north rail.

3. Mega Mall 2000

The ARCADE, TV-RAMA and its FOOD court, a hover-rink downstairs, and a loading dock behind the STAFF ONLY door. The keycard is in the laser display case at TV-RAMA.

pages.head: More Levels
pages.html:
4. The Teleport-A-Phone Exchange

Every booth in the world goes through here, and half of them are wrong numbers: Grandma's condo in Florida, the inside of a TV set, the bottom of the sea, the Jurassic period. Every room has quarters, so keep dialing. Booth number 4 is out of order. In the corner, the Restoring the Signal exhibit has a 1916 crank phone (go on, ring it) and a teletype that keeps typing the same tip, with no phone line at all.

5. The Moon

Moon buggies, the Crater Cafe (dinner in one pill), friendly aliens and an afternoon meteor shower. The Moon Pass is at the Visitor Center at the top of meteor alley; the Moon School airlock is up and to the right.

6. The Science Fair

Sparky is running around the gym with the cover page in his mouth, and the volcano projects are erupting. Zap him three times. Each zap changes his game: first he roams, then he plays keep-away (corner him against a project or a wall), then he gets the zoomies. He never bites, but the lava stings. After the third zap he gets dizzy and drops the page. Pick it up quickly, and don't zap it! Then turn in 20 pages at the judges' table, hand over the cover, and step up to the podium. Short of pages? Stand at the copier's tray by the signs: it prints a page every few seconds.

pages.head: Tips from the Future
pages.html:
• Always keep one quarter for the phone booth. Arcade games are fun, but they eat quarters.
  • If you run out of quarters at the phone exchange, every room has more - and they come back each time you dial.
  • Robots that chase you are slower than you are. Lead them around, then zap them.
  • Look both ways on the Superhighway. Trucks are slow; the teal cars are not.
  • Laser fences stay off longer than they stay on. Wait for the click, then go.
  • Pages count across all the levels. You don't need every single one.
  • Careful with the Zapper near the cover page: a zap will burn it up! If that happens, you'll have to start the level over.
  • Friendly aliens are worth a detour when you're hurt.

About this game

In The Year 2000! was made with GAME-MAKER 3.0 by Recreational Software Designs. Design, pictures, music and robot dog: Claude, for Sandbox Software.
